estimates.title: Published “astrology market” estimates conflict by orders of magnitude
estimates.sub: We anchor on the one methodologically consistent primary series — IBISWorld's US Psychic Services industry — and treat vendor projections as projections.

items.label: Horoscope apps only
items.tip: The narrowest definition: paid horoscope-app revenue only.

items.label: US psychic services
items.tip: IBISWorld NAICS OD4413 — 5.5% CAGR to 2025, 103,340 businesses. The number we build against.

items.label: “Broad astrology market”
items.tip: Definitions vary wildly; treat as directional at best.

items.label: Astrology & tarot by 2033
items.tip: A ~25% CAGR vendor projection — a hope, not a fact.

estimates.note: Bars share one linear scale deliberately: the spread is the finding. “Market size” claims in this category are a definitional choice, not a measurement.

who.title: Who actually engages
who.source: FIG. 02 · Pew Research Center, May 2025 · n=9,593
who.sub: Demand skews young, female, and LGBT — stable and mainstream rather than fringe or exploding.
who.note: Religious affiliation barely predicts engagement: 27% of Christians consult horoscopes vs 30% of the unaffiliated.

depth.title: Engagement is wide, not deep — and that's the design constraint
depth.sub: Most engagement is “just for fun.” The practitioners we equip serve the committed core — and grow the middle.

items.label: Rely a lot on it for major decisions

depth.note: A flat, wide market rewards the supply side: tools, productivity, and trust — not another consumer app fighting for the same 6%.

proof.title: What the benchmarks prove
proof.sub: Annual revenue, latest credibly reported. CHANI is the emphasis for a reason: all-human, ad-free, and still at scale — evidence that “human-made” commands willingness to pay.

items.label: AstroTalk
items.tip: FY24 revenue ₹651 crore, up 2.3× YoY and profitable — proof verified-practitioner marketplaces reach venture scale.

items.label: Nebula (OBRIO)
items.tip: Bootstrapped inside Genesis; among the top-grossing horoscope apps in the US.

items.label: CHANI
items.tip: Inc.-estimated ~$14M/yr, ~$11.99/mo subscriptions, 1M+ monthly readers, explicit zero-AI editorial policy.

proof.note: Figures are the latest credibly reported and not directly comparable (revenue vs ARR vs estimates). CHANI's is an Inc. estimate reported secondhand — flagged low-confidence in our market map.

commoditization.title: What AI does to generic interpretive work
commoditization.source: FIG. 05 · SoA 2024 · Bloomberry · Demirci et al. 2024
commoditization.sub: Three adjacent language crafts, measured post-ChatGPT. Generic work is commoditized; relationship-, brand-, and provenance-based work holds. That asymmetry is our entire thesis.

items.label: Translators who already lost work to genAI
Freelance writing demand
items.sub: Demirci et al. · within 8 months of ChatGPT

commoditization.note: An Oxford study attributed ~28,000 lost US translator jobs to machine translation. Stock photography followed the same curve — agencies now sell training data, not photos.
